The market that brings the greatest amount of choice at the lowest cost will be the least regulated market within a domain of property rights and rule of law.  

The free market has responded and incredibly it is growing, but it does so as an option in addition to the unwieldy government induced chaos.   Companies need to let employees op-out of their healthcare coverage and receive the difference in their paycheck.  They can then directly procure their chosen package.  Create an option to op-out of Federal healthcare.

There are several established healthcare models offered by private practices that emphasize extended face time with your chosen provider, personalized service, and direct payment structures that operate entirely outside of insurance companies and government programs like Medicare or Medicaid. These models prioritize accessibility, continuity of care, and reduced administrative burdens for both patients and physicians. The two most prominent are Direct Primary Care (DPC) and Concierge Medicine (also known as retainer medicine).  Is there greater patient, physician trust among those using DPC than company or government offered alternatives?

Catastrophic coverage is still needed, but this is “insurable”.

DPC practices doubled from 2017–2023, with continued expansion as of 2025.

Our health freedom was lost when the Federal Government took control.  This gross display of rampant corruption will only get worse as the absurdity of politicians’ “selflessness, benevolence”, and  omnipotence continues on display.

Medicare and Medicaid 1965, Affordable Care Act 2010…. and trending worse.  Transition companies out of Insurance like pensions to 401K’s. The Federalist Papers (1787–1788) did not discuss healthcare, food supply, or agriculture as federal responsibilities because these were seen as intimate, local concerns best handled by individuals, communities, or state governments. The Constitution, as defended by Hamilton, Madison, and Jay, deliberately limited federal powers to enumerated areas like defense, foreign affairs, and interstate commerce (Federalist No. 45). The framers assumed that issues affecting daily life: health, food, farming fell under state or private purview, reflecting a distrust of centralized control over personal matters.
